zh.summary: 用同一收件任務區分人機互動、介面與整體使用經驗，找到該改善的問題與需要的證據。
objectives: 以工作情境區分 HCI、UI 與 UX 的分析範圍。
指出美觀、易用與整體任務結果之間的差異。
為一個介面困難提出可觀察的修改假設。

readingGuide.goal: 以工作情境區分 HCI、UI 與 UX 的分析範圍。
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md、文字編輯器與合成收件情境；不需要改程式或接觸真人。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 wireframe-notes.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: 一份包含三種分析觀點、具體修改假設及待驗方法的 wireframe-notes.md。

sections.heading: 用不同問題看同一個系統
paragraphs: HCI（Human–Computer Interaction，人機互動）研究人如何與互動技術一起工作，也包含設計與評估方法。SIGCHI 將這個領域描述為跨學科的研究與實務，涉及資訊、心理、設計等專業。本課用它提醒自己：人的理解、情境、操作限制與技術行為都要一起考慮。
UI（User Interface，使用者介面）是人用來操作與接收回饋的介面，例如欄位標籤、按鈕、閱讀順序與錯誤訊息；它不只包含配色。UX（User Experience，使用者經驗）則看使用者接觸服務與產品的整體經驗，可能從準備文件開始，直到匯出後交接。本課以三種觀點教學，不把它們當成互斥職稱或固定先後階段。

sections.heading: 像看自助寄件的不同層面
paragraphs: 自助寄件機的輸入欄位、按鈕和付款提示屬於介面。研究戴手套的人能否操作觸控、寄件者如何理解重量與費用，是人機互動可以處理的問題。即使機器很好按，若包裹交付後沒有收件確認，整段寄件經驗仍可能讓人困惑。
三者彼此影響。改按鈕文字是 UI 修改；選擇文字要根據對使用者理解的研究；是否改善寄件結果，還要看操作前後的服務。不能把三個名稱直接換成「研究、畫圖、滿意度」就認為責任已分清。

sections.heading: 把收件困難轉成三種可追問問題
paragraphs: NN/G 的 UX 定義強調整體接觸經驗，也明確區別 UI 與 UX。本課據此查看收件任務：即使表單易讀，若使用者不知道該去哪裡取得文件類型，仍可能無法完成工作。加入更漂亮的圖示不會自動提供缺少的資料。
下面的問題都是教學假設，還沒有真人研究。你可以先選一個最影響任務的困難，再用訪談、任務觀察或介面測試取得適當證據。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜同一收件任務的三種觀點
blocks.description: 三張卡並列比較分析問題，沒有先研究完 HCI 才能開始 UI 的固定順序。

items.title: HCI：理解互動
items.body: 第一次使用的人，如何判斷「欄位齊全」與「正式受理」的差別？需要觀察其理解與操作。

items.title: UI：安排操作
items.body: 欄位有持續可見的名稱嗎？缺漏訊息是否指向文件類型與修正動作？

items.title: UX：看整段任務
items.body: 資料從哪裡準備、缺件由誰補、報告交給誰？畫面以外的交接也可能是阻礙。

sections.heading: 將外觀、易用與工作結果分開檢查
paragraphs: 視覺一致、文字清楚能幫助閱讀，但「看起來專業」不能代替使用者能否發現缺漏、回復錯誤與取得正確當次報告的證據。易用性關心人在特定情境中是否能學會、操作並完成任務；整體 UX 還包含其他接觸與期待。
NN/G 的易用性原則可以協助檢查系統狀態、使用者語言與錯誤復原；它們是啟發式方向，不是保證通過的評分公式。套用原則後仍應做任務試用，不以設計者覺得好看就結案。

sections.heading: 選與問題相符的證據
paragraphs: 若問題是「文件類型」名稱難懂，可請使用者解釋他認為這欄要填什麼，並觀察他找資料的過程。若問題是表單不能用鍵盤送出，就直接測試鍵盤路徑。若問題是交接後仍需重填，則需看報告接收者的工作。
同一方法不會回答所有問題。功能測試可以證明指定缺件案例被阻擋，不能證明人知道怎麼補；一次訪談可以揭露一種說法，不能證明每個人都如此。保留任務、情境與證據範圍，再決定下一個修改。

sections.heading: 留下一個能驗證的設計假設
paragraphs: 常見誤解是「UX 就是 UI 美化」。可以改用具體目標：「讓第一次使用者在看到缺漏後，能找到文件類型欄並知道要補什麼。」這個目標把文字、位置與行為接在一起，也能指向下一次任務觀察。
將候選設計寫進 wireframe-notes.md，再帶到 M04-02 的任務分析。下面示範只有設計假設，沒有宣稱觀察已發生。

blocks.heading: 三種觀點的工作筆記
paragraphs: 將以下合成範例放入 wireframe-notes.md，依你的課堂情境修改；這不是實際單位規定或研究結果。
blocks.code:
# 收件任務的設計假設（合成）
HCI 問題：使用者如何理解完整與受理的差別？
UI 候選：把「成功」改為「三個必要欄位已齊全」
UX 問題：取得報告後，接手者還需要什麼資訊？
待驗方法：指定缺件修正任務，加上交接角色訪談
目前證據：教學假設，未做真人研究
下一步：列出操作、判斷與例外，再畫線框稿

exercise.environment: problem.md、文字編輯器與合成收件情境；不需要改程式或接觸真人。
steps: 用同一缺件任務各寫一個 HCI、UI 與 UX 問題，保留操作前後的情境。
選一項困難，提出介面修改假設，說明要用什麼證據判斷。
將假設放入 wireframe-notes.md，和同儕核對是否把美觀或程式通過誤當成整體任務改善；單人可依檢核題自查。
exercise.expected: 一份包含三種分析觀點、具體修改假設及待驗方法的 wireframe-notes.md。
exercise.check: 能解釋三種觀點如何重疊；每個問題都有可觀察情境，沒有虛構研究結果。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成標記與未知，移除真人姓名、案件內容與沒有用途的個人描述。

en.summary: Use one intake task to distinguish human–computer interaction, the interface and the overall user experience, identifying problems to improve and the evidence needed.
objectives: Distinguish the scope of HCI, UI and UX through a work situation.
Identify differences among appearance, usability and overall task outcomes.
Propose an observable design hypothesis for an interface difficulty.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish the scope of HCI, UI and UX through a work situation.
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md, a text editor and a synthetic intake scenario; no code changes or actual participants are needed.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand wireframe-notes.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: wireframe-notes.md with three analytical perspectives, a concrete design hypothesis and a planned verification method.

sections.heading: Ask Different Questions About the Same System
paragraphs: Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) studies how people work with interactive technology, including methods for design and evaluation. SIGCHI describes an interdisciplinary research and practice community involving computing, psychology and design, among other fields. Here, that perspective reminds us to consider understanding, context, operating constraints and technical behavior together.

The User Interface (UI) is how people act and receive feedback: field labels, buttons, reading order and errors, not just colors. User Experience (UX) covers the broader experience with a service or product, potentially from preparing documents through handoff after export. These are teaching perspectives, not mutually exclusive job titles or fixed successive phases.

sections.heading: Examine Different Aspects of a Self-Service Parcel Kiosk
paragraphs: The kiosk’s fields, buttons and payment feedback belong to its interface. Whether gloved users can operate the touchscreen and how senders understand weight and charges are HCI questions. Even with easy controls, a missing receipt confirmation can leave the overall parcel-sending experience confusing.

The perspectives interact. Changing button wording is a UI change; choosing wording should draw on research into understanding. Assessing the shipping outcome also requires examining the surrounding service. Relabeling the three terms as “research, drawing and satisfaction” does not fully define responsibilities.

sections.heading: Turn an Intake Difficulty into Three Investigable Questions
paragraphs: NN/G’s UX definition covers the overall interaction experience and explicitly distinguishes UI from UX. Apply that distinction: a readable form may still leave users unable to obtain document-type information. More attractive icons do not supply the missing data.

The questions below are teaching assumptions without actual participant research. Choose a difficulty that materially affects the task, then obtain suitable evidence through interviews, task observation or interface testing.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Three Perspectives on One Intake Task
blocks.description: The cards compare analytical questions in parallel. UI work need not wait for a separate, completed HCI phase.

items.title: HCI: understanding interaction
items.body: How does a first-time user distinguish complete fields from official acceptance? Observe understanding and operation.

items.title: UI: arranging actions
items.body: Do fields have persistent names? Does missing-input feedback identify document type and how to correct it?

items.title: UX: examining the whole task
items.body: Where is data prepared, who supplies missing information and who receives the report? Handoffs outside the screen may be barriers.

sections.heading: Check Appearance, Usability and Outcomes Separately
paragraphs: Consistent visuals and clear wording aid reading, but a professional appearance cannot establish that people find omissions, recover from errors and obtain a correct report matching current input. Usability concerns learning, operation and task completion in a context; UX also includes other interactions and expectations.

NN/G’s heuristics help inspect status, user language and recovery. They are broad inspection principles, not a scoring formula guaranteeing success. Test tasks after applying them instead of accepting a design because the designer likes its appearance.

sections.heading: Choose Evidence That Answers the Question
paragraphs: If “document type” is unclear, ask users to explain what they think belongs there and observe how they find it. If keyboard submission fails, test that keyboard path. If handoff still requires re-entry, examine the report recipient’s work.

No single method answers everything. Functional tests can establish blocking of specified missing-input cases, not whether people know how to correct them. One interview reveals an account, not a universal experience. Retain task, context and evidence limits before selecting the next change.

sections.heading: Retain a Verifiable Design Hypothesis
paragraphs: A common mistake is equating UX with visual UI polish. Use a concrete goal: “After seeing missing-input feedback, first-time users can locate document type and understand what to provide.” This connects wording, position and behavior to a later task observation.
Record the candidate in wireframe-notes.md for M04-02 task analysis. The example contains design hypotheses only; it does not claim observations have occurred.

blocks.heading: Notes from Three Perspectives
paragraphs: The original Traditional Chinese template records the completeness/acceptance HCI question, a UI wording change from “success” to “three required fields are complete,” a UX handoff question, planned task/interview methods, synthetic evidence status and the next analysis step. Adapt it in wireframe-notes.md; it is not an actual rule or research finding.
blocks.code:
# 收件任務的設計假設（合成）
HCI 問題：使用者如何理解完整與受理的差別？
UI 候選：把「成功」改為「三個必要欄位已齊全」
UX 問題：取得報告後，接手者還需要什麼資訊？
待驗方法：指定缺件修正任務，加上交接角色訪談
目前證據：教學假設，未做真人研究
下一步：列出操作、判斷與例外，再畫線框稿

exercise.environment: problem.md, a text editor and a synthetic intake scenario; no code changes or actual participants are needed.
steps: Write one HCI, UI and UX question for the same missing-information task, retaining its surrounding context.
Choose one difficulty and propose an interface-change hypothesis with evidence to judge it.
Record the hypothesis in wireframe-notes.md. With a peer, check whether appearance or passing code was mistaken for overall task improvement; independent learners can use the checks.
exercise.expected: wireframe-notes.md with three analytical perspectives, a concrete design hypothesis and a planned verification method.
exercise.check: Explain how the perspectives overlap. Every question has an observable situation without invented research results.
exercise.cleanup: Keep synthetic labels and unknowns. Remove actual names, case content and unnecessary personal descriptions.

zh.prompt: 哪個例子最能表達 UX 比畫面更廣？
options: 表單配色已統一，所以整段服務必定好用
按鈕加陰影就完成 UX
表單操作清楚，但匯出後接手者仍不知道如何使用報告，需要查看整段交接
只有程式碼行數影響 UX
rationales: 視覺一致不代表整段工作完成。
視覺效果不能代替任務與情境證據。
操作前後的交接也是整體經驗的一部分。
程式碼行數不能單獨描述使用者經驗。

en.prompt: Which example best shows that UX extends beyond the screen?
options: Consistent form colors guarantee an easy overall service.
Adding shadows to buttons completes UX.
The form is clear, but the next worker still cannot use its report; examine the whole handoff.
Only code line counts affect UX.
rationales: Visual consistency does not establish end-to-end task completion.
Visual effects cannot replace task and context evidence.
Handoffs before and after interaction are part of the overall experience.
Line counts alone do not describe user experience.

zh.prompt: 下列哪個 UI 問題可直接檢查？
options: 所有人是否喜歡這個組織
錯誤訊息是否指出缺少文件類型與如何修正
整個產業的資訊文化如何形成
研究是否一定能保證成功
rationales: 範圍過廣，也無法直接由介面判定。
文字、關聯與修正提示是具體介面安排。
這不是直接的介面檢查。
研究能減少未知，不能保證所有設計成功。

en.prompt: Which UI question can be inspected directly?
options: Does everyone like this organization?
Does the error identify missing document type and explain correction?
How did the entire industry’s information culture develop?
Does research always guarantee success?
rationales: This is too broad to determine from the interface alone.
Wording, association and correction guidance are concrete interface decisions.
This is not a direct interface inspection.
Research reduces unknowns but guarantees no universal design success.

zh.prompt: 缺件測試全數通過後，可以宣稱什麼？
options: 所有人都能自行補件
正式受理流程已完成
UX 已完全驗證
指定程式案例符合規則；理解與操作仍需適當任務證據
rationales: 程式測試沒有直接觀察人的理解。
完整性檢查與正式受理不同。
整體 UX 還有測試範圍外的問題。
結論與證據範圍一致，也指出下一步。

en.prompt: All missing-input tests pass. What can be claimed?
options: Everyone can correct omissions independently.
Official acceptance is implemented.
UX is fully verified.
Specified program cases follow the rules; understanding and operation still need suitable task evidence.
rationales: Program tests do not directly observe understanding.
Completeness checking and official acceptance differ.
Overall UX includes questions outside these tests.
This matches the claim to the evidence and identifies the next step.
